discovery: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO magnetic tunnel junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

nominees.name: Shinji Yuasa
nominees.affiliation: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Tsukuba, Japan

motivation: In 2001 Butler and co-workers predicted that coherent tunnelling through crystalline MgO barriers would filter electron states by wavefunction symmetry, giving enormous spin polarization. In 2004 Parkin and Yuasa independently showed this experimentally: Fe(Co)/MgO/Fe(Co) junctions had room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance of about 200 percent, several times higher than amorphous-barrier junctions, and later results passed 600 percent. This was a new physical principle, symmetry-filtered spin-dependent tunnelling, and it was quickly turned into technology. Within a few years MgO junctions were used in every hard-disk read head, and today they are the storage element of spin-transfer-torque MRAM made in leading foundries. Their output signal makes nonvolatile, energy-efficient memory and logic possible. Few discoveries in condensed-matter physics have gone so directly from a quantum-mechanical insight to products used by billions of people.
